title: The Deceptions of Demons and the Remedy of Anger
english: …the demons fear, as [they fear] gentleness; for that Moses too possessed it, being called meek above all men (Num 12:3). And holy David too declared it worthy of God’s remembrance, saying: ‘Remember, Lord, David and all his gentleness’ (Ps 132:1). But the Savior Himself commanded us to become imitators of His gentleness, saying: ‘Learn from Me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls’ (Matt 11:29). But if anyone abstains from foods and drinks, yet provokes thumos with evil thoughts, he is like a ship sailing the sea with a demon as pilot; wherefore one must attend as much as possible to our dog, and teach him to destroy only the wolves and not to devour the sheep, showing all gentleness toward all men.

Chapter 15. Alone among the thoughts, that of vainglory is manifold, encompassing almost the whole inhabited world and opening the doors to all the demons, like some evil traitor of a good city. Wherefore it greatly humbles the recluse’s mind, filling him with many words and affairs, and ruining his prayers — through which he strives to heal all the wounds of his soul. All the demons, having been defeated, augment this thought, and again through it they all gain entrance into souls, making the last things truly worse than the first. From this thought is born also that one of pride, which shook down from heaven to earth the seal of likeness and the crown of beauty.

But leap away from this, and do not linger, lest we betray our life to others and our life to the unmerciful. Intense prayer puts this demon to flight, as does doing nothing willingly that contributes to the accursed glory. When the mind of the recluses lays hold of a little dispassion, then, having acquired a horse of vainglory, it immediately gallops through the cities, glutted with unmixed praise from glory, whom, by dispensation, the spirit of fornication meets and shuts into one of the pigsties, teaching him not to leave his bed before perfect health, nor to imitate the unruly among the sick, who, still carrying remnants of weakness within themselves, give themselves to roads and untimely baths, and fall into relapsing sicknesses.

Wherefore, sitting still, let us rather attend to ourselves, so that, progressing in virtue, we become hard to move toward evil, and being renewed in knowledge, we receive a multitude of varied contemplations, and being lifted up again in prayer, we shall more clearly behold the light of our Savior.

Chapter 16. I cannot write all the evildoings of the demons, and I am ashamed to enumerate their evil crafts, fearing the simpler among those who will read. But hear the craftiness of the spirit of fornication. When someone acquires dispassion in the desiring part, and the shameful thoughts henceforth become cooled down, then it brings in men and women sporting with one another, and makes the recluse a spectator of shameful deeds and postures. But this temptation is not among those that linger; for intense prayer, and a very strict diet with wakefulness, and the exercise of spiritual contemplations, drive him like a waterless cloud. Sometimes it even touches the flesh, levering it toward irrational burning, and this utterly wicked one contrives countless other devices, which it is not necessary to publish or hand over in writing. A boiling of thumos stirred up against the demon also contributes greatly against the thoughts — which thumos it especially fears when troubled over the thoughts and destroying its notions; and this is the ‘Be angry, and sin not’ (Eph 4:26). This is a useful medicine applied to the soul in such temptations. The demon of anger also imitates this demon, and fashions — he too — some of one’s parents or friends or relatives or household being insulted and beaten by the unworthy, and stirs up the thumos of the recluses, so that they may utter something evil or do something toward those appearing in the mind — to whom one must not attend, but must quickly snatch the mind away from such images, lest, lingering among them, he become at the time of prayer like a smoking firebrand. And the irascible fall into these temptations…
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sword of Discernment and the Deception of Gold
english: …and especially those easily kindled to fits of anger, who are far from pure prayer and from the knowledge of our Savior Jesus Christ.

Chapter 17. The Lord handed over the notions of this age to man, the good shepherd, as sheep; for He has, He says, put the age in his heart; having yoked to him thumos and desire for help, so that through thumos he might put to flight the notions of the wolves, and through desire he might love the sheep — though often assailed by rains and winds. And besides these He gave him pasture, that he might shepherd the sheep, and a place of grass, and water of rest, and a psaltery and a harp, and a rod and a staff, so that from this flock he might both be fed and clothed, and gather mountain hay. ‘For who, He says, shepherds a flock and does not eat of the milk of the flock?’ The recluse must, then, guard this flock by night and by day, lest any of the notions become beast-caught or fall among robbers; but if anything of the sort should happen in the glen, immediately snatch it from the mouth of the lion or the bear. The notion concerning a brother becomes beast-caught if it pastures with hatred what is in us; and that concerning a woman, if it turns among us with shameful desire; and that of silver and gold, if it lodges with greed. And the notions of the holy gifts, if they graze in the mind with vainglory; and likewise it will happen with the other notions, when they are stolen by the passions.

Chapter 18. One must keep these things not only in the day, but also guard them waking by night. For it happens that even one who phantasies shamefully and evilly loses his own; and this is what was said by holy Jacob: ‘I did not bring to you a beast-caught sheep; I paid back from myself thefts of the day and thefts of the night, and I was consumed by the burning heat of the day and the frost of the night, and sleep departed from my eyes’ (Gen 31:39–40). But if from toil acedia also comes upon us, let us run back a little to the rock of knowledge and converse with the psaltery, striking the strings of knowledge through the virtues, and let us again pasture the sheep under Mount Sinai, so that the God of our fathers may call us too from the bush and grant us also the words of the signs and wonders.

Christ raises the rational nature put to death by evil through the contemplation of all the ages; and His Father raises its dead soul through the death of Christ, by knowledge of Himself. And this is what is said by Paul: ‘If we died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him’ (Rom 6:8).

When the mind, having stripped off the old man, puts on the one from grace, then it will also see its own state at the time of prayer, like in color to sapphire or heaven, which Scripture also calls the place of God, seen by the elders under Mount Sinai.

Chapter 19. When one of the enemies, having approached, wounds you, and you wish to turn his sword, according to what is written, against his own heart, do thus, as we say. Divide up by yourself the thought cast by him — whatever it is, and of how many things it is composed, and which of them most afflicts the mind. What I mean is this: suppose the thought of love of money has been sent by him; divide it into the mind that received it, and into the notion of the gold, and into the gold itself, and into the money-loving passion; and then ask which of these is sin — the mind? And how? It is the image of God. Or the notion of the gold? And who in his right mind would ever say this? Or is the gold itself sin? And for whose sake did it come to be? It follows, then, that it is neither a thing subsisting in essence, nor a notion of a thing, nor again an incorporeal mind, but a certain misanthropic pleasure, born from free will, constraining the mind to use God’s creatures badly — which God’s law has been entrusted to circumcise.
And as you investigate these things, the thought will be destroyed, being analyzed into its own contemplation, and the demon will flee from you, your mind being lifted to a height by this knowledge.

title: The Deception of Demons and the Flight of Thoughts
english: …your shepherd’s bag, and seek the contemplation of this: how angels and demons approach our world, but we do not approach their worlds; for we can no longer join angels to God, nor do we choose to make demons more unclean. And how Lucifer, rising early, was cast down to the earth, and deems the sea as an ointment-jar, and Tartarus of the abyss as a captive, and boils the abyss like bronze, troubling all through his evil and wishing to rule all? For the contemplation of these things greatly wounds the demon and puts all his host to flight. But these things happen only to those gradually purified, who in some measure see the logoi of what has come to be. But the impure do not know the contemplation of these things, nor would they be heeded even if they chanted what they learned from others, since much dust and tumult arise through the passions in the war. For the host of the foreigners must by all means quiet down a little, so that Goliath alone may meet our David. Likewise let us use this division and this kind of war against all impure thoughts.

Chapter 21. Of the unclean demons, some tempt man as man, and others trouble man as an irrational animal; the first, approaching, cast into us notions of vainglory or pride or envy or accusation, which touch nothing of the irrational; but the second, drawing near, stir up thumos or desire contrary to nature. For these passions happen to be common to us and to the irrational animals, being covered by the rational nature. Wherefore the Holy Spirit also says to those falling into human thoughts: ‘I said: You are gods, and all sons of the Most High; but you die as men, and fall as one of the rulers’ (Ps 82:6). And to those moved irrationally, what does He say? ‘Do not become like a horse and mule, which have no understanding; with bit and bridle you must hold their jaws, who do not come near you’ (Ps 32:9).

But the soul that sins, it shall die. It is clear that men, dying as men, will be buried by men; but those put to death as irrational — that is, falling — will be eaten by vultures or crows, whose young, some call upon the Lord, while others are defiled in blood. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

Chapter 22. When some of the unclean thoughts are quickly put to flight, let us seek the cause whence this happened: whether because of the scarcity of the thing — the matter being hard to obtain — or because, through the dispassion present in us, the enemies had no strength against us? For example, if one of the recluses should be prompted by a demon to be entrusted with the spiritual governance of the first city, it is clear that he will not linger imagining this thought, and the cause becomes known from what is said; but if one becomes [entrusted] of any city whatever, and reckons likewise, such a one is blessed in dispassion. Likewise such a manner will be found when examined in the case of the other thoughts. These things one must know for our eagerness and power, so that we may see whether we have crossed the Jordan and are near the city of the Phoenicians, or still dwell in the desert and are beaten by the foreigners.

For the demon of love of money seems to me very manifold and resourceful for deception; often, when straitened by extreme renunciation, he immediately plays the steward and lover of the poor, and receives guests not yet present more genuinely, and sends service to others who are lacking, and visits the city prisons, and supposedly ransoms those being sold, and attaches himself to rich women, and points out those who ought to receive benefit, and again advises others who possess a fat purse to renounce it, and thus, having deceived the soul little by little, subjects it to thoughts of love of money, and hands it over to the demon of vainglory.

Chapter 23.
